correctness.rationale: The left and right branch derivative matrices are signed monomial; a word with t right visits induces permutation +t mod M with g=gcd(M,t) cycles. Each cycle product has 2-adic exponent t/g plus occupied left gaps of one residue class; thus eigenvalue modulus 2^((t+g ell_c)/M). Partitioning t+1 gaps into g residue classes gives the stated binomial weighted-composition histogram. When g=1 all moduli equal 2^(n/M), whereas g>=2 forces t>=p and min modulus >=2^(p/M); R^p L^(n-p) achieves the bound for n>p, and RL^(n-1) realizes splitting. Complement of all occupied classes at t=p yields E_M(n)=binom(n,p)-binom(n-p,p)-binom(n-p-1,p-1). Primary symbolic coding supplies one isolated point for each non-all-left word, not merely a formal word count. Independently checked 3514 signed-matrix words and 56 histogram cases; not a proof by finite sample.
